bugs: failed() uses $this->order->refresh(), which ignores the soft-delete scope, so a cancelled order whose job failed gets shipment_status=failed. Ops would see a false alarm (confirmed with a probe). app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:62
Retry-After on a 429 has no upper bound, so a partner that sends a large value can park the job until retryUntil (1h) runs out. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:141
antipatterns: No WithoutOverlapping lock. The Idempotency-Key header and the markAsPaid guard are the only protection against two copies of the job running at once. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:35
markAsPaid checks the paid status on the in-memory model, so a stale instance can dispatch the job twice. app/Models/Order.php:43
The nested if could be combined into one condition. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:51-55
strengths: Uses Laravel 13 job attributes on one line (Timeout, Backoff, MaxExceptions, DeleteWhenMissingModels) and keeps one useful why-comment about retryUntil
Treats 429 differently from other errors: release() honours Retry-After instead of counting as an exception
Claims the notification atomically (conditional update on shipment_notified_at) and rolls the claim back if sending fails, so the email goes out exactly once
Returns early on a 422 and records the reason without failing or retrying the job

Thorough Pest tests: withFakeQueueInteractions assertReleased/NotFailed, a real mail failure via the MessageSending event, the order serialized while queued then cancelled, Http::fakeSequence recovery, and the idempotency key

bugs: markAsPaid is not idempotent. Calling it on an order that is already paid or shipped dispatches the job again and resets shipment_status from sent to pending. The job then skips (the reference exists) and the status stays wrong (confirmed with a probe). app/Models/Order.php:39-49
failed() uses fresh(), which includes trashed rows, so a cancelled order can be marked failed. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:64
antipatterns: A 429 is thrown like a 5xx, so it uses the generic backoff and ignores Retry-After. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:97,116
Sends the email first and saves shipment_notified_at afterwards, with no atomic claim. If the save fails or two workers race, the email can go out twice. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:121-127
Tests call app()->call([$job,'handle']) directly instead of using withFakeQueueInteractions, so they never check release or fail. tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php:22-25
strengths: Modern Laravel 13 style: Backoff/MaxExceptions/Timeout attributes, the Foundation Queueable trait, the #[Fillable] attribute and enum casts
Treats every 4xx except 408 and 429 as permanent and calls $this->fail() with a reason that includes the HTTP status
Checks both trashed() and paid status before shipping; WithoutOverlapping and an account-wide RateLimited limiter
Sets preventStrayRequests globally in Pest.php; tests cover rollback (no dispatch), cancelled orders through real serialization, and a missing id

bugs: The job never checks that the order is paid, so dispatching it for a pending order ships it (confirmed with a probe). markAsPaid is the only dispatch path, so the risk is latent. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:50-66
Only 422 counts as permanent. A 400 or 401 is retried for up to 8 exceptions over 2 hours before ops see it. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:97
antipatterns: A 429 is thrown like a 5xx and Retry-After is ignored. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:105
The base tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php was deleted, an unrelated change
A test mixes Mail::shouldReceive with Mail::fake and resets container internals by hand (forgetInstance/clearResolvedInstance). tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php:193-203
Handles the 422 by calling fail() on an exception it builds itself, while a missing id throws RuntimeException; two styles for similar outcomes. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:98,110
strengths: Uses the variadic Backoff attribute plus DeleteWhenMissingModels, MaxExceptions and Timeout, with a short why-comment on retryUntil
refresh() at the start of handle and failed() using withTrashed()->find, so a cancelled order is left untouched
Atomic claim-then-send for the email, rolled back if sending fails
markAsPaid is guarded against redispatch; Http::baseUrl is used for the configured URL, and there is a test that the URL is configurable
Tests cover the sync-driver outage leading to failed, sequence recovery, and retrying only the email

bugs: markAsPaid queries withTrashed(), so a cancelled (soft-deleted) order can be marked paid and get a job dispatched. Nothing ships, but the order data is wrong (confirmed with a probe). app/Models/Order.php:54
antipatterns: Uses string class constants (STATUS_PAID, SHIPMENT_SENT) instead of backed enums with casts. app/Models/Order.php:19-27

Uses the four separate pre-Laravel-11 job traits instead of Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable, and properties ($maxExceptions, $timeout, $deleteWhenMissingModels) and backoff() instead of queue attributes. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:22-34,48
#[UseFactory] is redundant with conventional factory discovery. app/Models/Order.php:13
Comments add bulk and some just restate the code. app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:26,60; app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25
markAsPaid does a raw update and then forceFill()->syncOriginal() to fake the in-memory state; ceremony. app/Models/Order.php:54-69
Uses the old-style protected $fillable array instead of the #[Fillable] attribute
strengths: The strongest handling of the partner's failure modes: 429 releases with a capped Retry-After, 5xx and 408 are thrown, every other 4xx is recorded as failed with the status and reason, and a 201 with no id is marked failed instead of retried (which avoids a possible duplicate shipment)
markAsPaid claims the order atomically with a conditional update, so it is idempotent even from a stale instance
recordFailure uses the scoped query whereNull('shipment_reference'), so it never overwrites a sent shipment or touches a cancelled order
The best tests: a real database-queue afterCommit rollback test, an end-to-end rate-limit test with freezeTime/travel, assertReleased(delay: 7), and describe() blocks

v.rationale:
All four test suites pass: impl-2 22 tests, impl-3 20, impl-4 24, impl-1 25. I probed at least two edge cases in each and deleted the probes afterwards. Every implementation uses afterCommit dispatch, an account-wide perSecond(5) limiter, connect and request timeouts, an Idempotency-Key header, retryUntil plus MaxExceptions, and a failed() hook that records the reason.

The ranking comes down to these differences:

1. impl-1 combines modern Laravel 13 idioms (attributes, enums, #[Fillable]) with the best 429 handling (release honouring Retry-After) and an atomic exactly-once email claim. Its tests are the most idiomatic. It lacks a WithoutOverlapping lock, and its failed() can flag a cancelled order as failed; both are minor.
2. impl-4 is the most robust against the partner: an atomic idempotent markAsPaid, Retry-After capped, all 4xx errors surfaced to ops, a missing id treated as failed to avoid duplicates, and the best tests (real database-queue afterCommit, rate limiting under frozen time). It loses points for dated idioms (string constants instead of enums, legacy job traits, properties instead of attributes, redundant #[UseFactory], heavy comments). Its withTrashed markAsPaid can mark a cancelled order paid.
3. impl-3 is clean and modern, refreshes the order and uses withTrashed in failed(), and claims the email atomically. It ignores Retry-After on 429, treats only 422 as permanent, and its job doesn't check that the order is paid. One test mixes mocks with fakes awkwardly, and it deleted ExampleTest.
4. impl-2 is modern and tidy but has the clearest bug: markAsPaid is not idempotent. Re-calling it redispatches the job and resets a sent shipment to pending, and the status stays wrong (confirmed with a probe). It also sends the email before saving the notified flag, with no atomic claim.
